applicable_when: The kernel performs a layout permutation from NCHW (contiguous) to a strided NHWC-like format. Loads from in_ptr0 are contiguous in x2 (stride-1), making them vectorizable with tl.max_contiguous/tl.multiple_of hints so the compiler emits 128-bit (float4) loads instead of scalar 32-bit loads. This directly reduces L1TEX pressure and scoreboard stall cycles (46.4% of all stall cycles). Additionally, the current XBLOCK=128 produces only 0.74 waves/SM (1568 CTAs across 132 SMs), leaving the GPU severely underutilized. Increasing XBLOCK to 512 reduces the grid to ~392 CTAs but each CTA does 4x more work per launch, improving instruction-level parallelism and hiding L1TEX latency via more in-flight memory requests per warp. The store pattern (y0 + 3*x2) has inherent stride-3 scatter that cannot be fully coalesced without algorithmic restructuring, but vectorizing loads and increasing tile size will reduce the relative cost of the store overhead.
